configuration.study_note: Separate, unexecuted fresh Rust-only follow-up after the complete powered comparison. Its saved Rust 120,000-user attempt was generator-invalid from actual sampler/wake delays and remains invalid; the earlier 110,000-user local PASS is a short diagnostic only and is not reused as a new phase or rescued into a capacity score. The 110,000 start and 115,000 ceiling are selected before new data to keep the native generator near that observed headroom boundary. Use the unchanged v3 controller, Rust binary/source/env, 8 CPU/16 GiB target, separate 8 CPU/8 GiB client, dedicated_client_cgroup_v1 policy and all native timing/SLO/clock/identity guards. Start one new full-seed clone and one fresh continuous session with the original 10,000-user 60+120-second warmup; perform fresh probes and 60+300-second holds only. A valid 115,000 PASS goes to a five-minute hold at the ceiling and establishes only a held-user LOWER BOUND, never a maximum. A valid 115,000 SLO failure may bracket a 110,000 hold, but any generator/clock invalidity stops without a failed server bound. Prior raw/results stay unchanged. A censored Rust lower bound alone cannot establish a Goose or first-place advantage. Execute only after the powered balanced comparison has finished, under the same powered/awake condition.

protocol.rounding_policy: local search: two significant digits; bisection uses strict integer midpoint if rounded midpoint hits either bound
protocol.database_policy: one fresh full-seed clone and one continuous app session per implementation; no reset between warmup/probes/holds
protocol.invalid_policy: retain and stop that implementation; invalid phases never enter pass/fail brackets or receive a score; no selective retry
